transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. Um, I'm here because... well, I guess I just have a lot of energy, which is usually a great thing, right? But lately, I feel like I'm just always running hot. It's like I can't quite shut the motor off. 

And, um, I'm a firefighter, so you'd think that would be helpful, but... well, if I'm being honest, it's actually been getting me into a little bit of trouble at the firehouse recently. Nothing too crazy, I just... I really want to make sure I'm doing my best and not causing issues for the guys. Does that make sense for why I'd come in?
Can you tell me more about this increased energy you mentioned — have you noticed it lasting for days at a time without needing much sleep, or feeling like your thoughts are racing?

Oh, um, no, it's not really like that. I definitely still need my sleep. I mean, shift work at the station messes with your schedule a bit, obviously, but I don't go days without sleeping or anything extreme like that. I'm pretty normal that way, I think. 

And as for my thoughts... I wouldn't say they're *racing*, exactly. That makes it sound a little intense. It's more just... I guess I just always have a few things bouncing around in my head? But it's nothing bad, I promise. I just like to stay busy and keep things moving. 

Is... is that the kind of thing you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and not making it sound worse than it is.
Have you found yourself acting impulsively or taking risks lately — like doing things without thinking through the consequences?

Oh, gosh, no. No, definitely not. I mean, especially with my job, you really can't be reckless, right? We have protocols for a reason, and I always try to follow them. 

I wouldn't say I do things without thinking about the consequences... maybe I'm just a little spontaneous sometimes? Like, I might jump in and start a project around the station before anyone asks, but it's never anything dangerous or risky. I really try to be mindful of how my actions affect the rest of the crew. I'm actually a pretty responsible guy, I promise. 

Is... is that okay? I just really don't want you to get the impression that I'm out of control or anything like that. I always try to do the right thing.
Have you noticed yourself getting more irritable or emotionally reactive lately — like feeling frustrated or annoyed more easily than usual?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I'm irritable. I mean, the firehouse can be a high-stress environment, you know? Sometimes things get a little tense, but I try really hard not to let it get to me. I definitely don't want to be that guy who's snapping at everyone or bringing the mood down. 

I guess... maybe I get a little flustered sometimes if things aren't moving fast enough, but I wouldn't call it angry or anything. I just like to keep the momentum going. But I always try to keep a smile on my face and be a good team player. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound like I'm difficult to work with, because I really do get along great with the guys.
Do you find it hard to focus on tasks or get easily distracted, especially when you're trying to finish something important at work or at home?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? But I don't think it's anything too unusual. The firehouse is just a really busy place, you know? There's always something going on. 

So, yeah, if I'm trying to finish up a report or something, it can be... a little tricky to stay completely locked in. Like, a radio chirp might go off, or someone will walk past the bay, or... or even just a thought about a call we had yesterday will pop into my head. And then I guess I kind of get knocked off what I was doing. It does take me a little while to get back on track sometimes. 

But I always get my work done! I really do. I just might take a little longer or have to restart a few times. It's not like I'm ignoring my responsibilities or anything like that. I really hope that doesn't make me sound incompetent. I just have a lot going on around me, you know? Is that... is that pretty normal for someone in my line of work?
Do you feel physically restless or have a need to keep moving, even when you're trying to sit still or focus on something?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I'm bouncing off the walls or anything. I know how to be professional. But... I guess I do prefer to be on my feet. 

When we have those long command meetings, and I'm just sitting there in a chair... I don't know, it sometimes feels like my engine is just revving a little too high? Like my body is telling me I should be up, walking the bay, checking the rigs... really just doing anything other than staying planted in that one spot. 

But I don't disrupt the meetings! I stay seated, I really do. I just... I might shift around a bit or tap my foot. I think it's just because I'm so used to being active on the job, you know? It's a physical job. So sitting still just feels a little unnatural sometimes. That doesn't mean I'm hyper or anything, right? I just like to stay productive.
How long have you felt this way — does this restlessness and difficulty staying focused go back further than just your time at the firehouse, maybe even to when you were in school or earlier in life?

Well, um... I guess it does go back a bit. I really don't want to make it sound like I was a bad kid or a troublemaker, because I wasn't at all! I always respected my teachers and wanted to do a good job. 

But... yeah, my mom says I was actually a lot like this back in grade school, too. She always reminds me how I was constantly popping out of my seat, or... or I'd be blurting out answers before the teacher even finished asking the question. I think I was just really eager to participate, you know? And I did tend to lose my homework a lot, which meant I got a fair amount of notes sent home. 

But my teachers always made sure to tell my mom that I was bright enough to do the work! I really was smart enough, I just... maybe had a little trouble channeling all that energy into the right places. That's pretty normal for boys at that age, right? Just being a little overly enthusiastic? I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a problem student.
Can you recall if these feelings of restlessness or difficulty staying focused were present before you were 12 years old, such as during early childhood or elementary school years?

Well, um... yeah, like I was just mentioning, it definitely goes back to when I was pretty young. Probably way before I was 12. 

My mom actually still brings it up sometimes, how I was in grade school. She says I was always the kid who couldn't stay in his seat, or... or I'd just shout out the answers in class. I guess I just got really excited and wanted to be involved? I didn't mean to be disruptive, I promise. 

And, um, I did lose my homework quite a bit back then. The teachers would send notes home to my mom about it. But they always told her I was smart! They knew I could do the work, I just... I guess I had a hard time keeping track of all the papers and sitting still for long periods. 

That’s... that’s not too unusual for a little kid, though, right? I think a lot of boys are just full of energy like that. I really hope it doesn't sound like I was a difficult child. I always tried my best to be good.
